transcription.notes: Typed figures; the typeface confuses 5, 6 and 8. Group 40 corrected to 88789 (not 88769) and group 20 to 8918 (not 6918) on full-resolution crops. Readings such as 06887, 4118 and 0089 fit the glyph forms but are not certain; repeated groups were read the same way every time.

documents.route: Washington -> Berlin (German Embassy -> Auswärtiges Amt, via the State Department and the American Embassy in Berlin)

plaintext.source: Not found. Not in Bernstorff 1920 or the Official German Documents (1923). Probably the second subject named in Lansing's letter of 10 Jan 1917 (FRUS 1917 Supp. 1 doc. 75): the American note of 18 Dec 1916 on peace terms. Not confirmed.

transcription.notes: Group 447 (sheet 2, row 12, second group) has its second figure typed over: 28648 or 26648 [?]. Group 377 is the only six-figure group, 108609 [?]. Struck groups on the sheets are kept in transcription.txt in braces and not counted.

system.summary: Two-part (randomised) numerical code of four-figure groups 0000-9999 with leading zeros kept; five-figure groups are a prefix figure plus a four-figure base group that changes the form of the word; several groups for the full stop; by route, date and structure the German diplomatic Code 7500 (also written 0075) of Friedman and Mendelsohn 1938, which does not name this cable.
system.sibling_key: Code 7500 (also written 0075): Friedman and Mendelsohn 1938, p. 16 and n. 40, give the Bernstorff messages on this State Department route as a two-part code of 10,000 phrases numbered 0000-9999; this cable is not in their list; no copy of the code was available; not code 13040, whose 19 Jan 1917 Zimmermann text is mostly five-figure groups in the 10000-24000 range.
system.notes: distinct_symbols = distinct groups as written in the whole message (404). homophones: at least three groups for the full stop (1515, 3377, 0404; 1724 probably a stop or paragraph), and the prefix figure gives several groups per word. nomenclator.entries = the 82 base groups fixed from telegram No. 205; unread_groups = the groups inside No. 205 (groups 0-146) with no value of their own: the five head groups, 0278 at the end, 7918, and the unsplit runs 19-23, 28-30, 59-63 and 125-131 (27 groups). The 'prefix 8 = past participle' rule rests on two secure cases (86699 vorgegangen, 88789 herbeigeführt); 85380 = geantwortet in part 2 is a guess. Prefix 5 (54873 = Vereinigten Staaten, against plain 4873) has no known meaning. The groups are not in alphabetical order, so the code is two-part.

prior_solution.where: The German text of telegram No. 205 (groups 0-146) is printed by Bernstorff, Deutschland und Amerika (1920), pp. 325-326, and in English in the Official German Documents (1923), vol. II, p. 1017. Neither links it to the ciphertext in NARA 763.72111/4443 or gives code groups. No decipherment of the ciphertext and no Room 40 decrypt was found in a light web search; not consulted: Boghardt, The Zimmermann Telegram (2012), on the State Department route and Room 40's handling of Bernstorff's Jan 1917 traffic; TNA HW 7 and ADM 137; PA AA. Since the British read the State Department cables and 0075 was partly broken, a Room 40 decrypt may exist; 'not found in print' and 'first link made here' are qualified claims until Boghardt is checked. Nothing found for groups 147-576.

conditions.human_role: Outside contribution (WAINUT): the operator chose the catalogue item; transcription, the search for the printed text, the alignment, the controls and an independent check were done by AI language-model agents and checked against the NARA images. No hand correction of readings recorded.
tools: decode.py (decryption from codebook.tsv and align_205.tsv; span check; blind alignment test with controls; prefix-figure test)
models: AI language-model agents (WAINUT); a vision-capable language model for the transcription

solution.what: Fetched NARA M367 roll 166 (naId 27179174) frames 0769-0795: memorandum in clear (0769-0775), its translation (0778-0784), the cipher on two typed sheets (0785, 0786), Lansing's note and the 'Please deliver following cipher' telegram of 11 Jan 1917 (0787-0789). Frame 0786 is sheet 2, not a reversed image.
Transcribed 577 groups (505 four-figure, 67 five-figure, 4 three-figure, 1 six-figure); the catalogue's 'about 150 groups' was too low.

Group census: in 21 of the 67 five-figure groups the last four figures occur as a four-figure group (about 2.2 expected by chance; first four figures: 2). Five-figure groups read as a prefix figure plus a base group.

The catalogue's suggested crib, the German memorandum filed in clear (frames 0769-0775), was set aside: the memorandum is what telegram No. 205 reports on, and the cipher aligns with No. 205 itself (below). No group-by-group test of the memorandum text was recorded.

Found Bernstorff's own telegram No. 205 of 10 Jan 1917 ('Antwort auf Telegramm 148': memorandum handed to Lansing, warning of a break with the United States) printed in Deutschland und Amerika (1920), pp. 325-326, and in English in the Official German Documents (1923) II p. 1017; FRUS 1917 Supp. 1 doc. 75 says the message was sent the next day.

Aligned groups 0-146 with telegram No. 205 word for word: every repeated group falls on a repeated word (Lansing, Wilson, mit, wird, von, bis, er, muß, auf, werden, ist, im Sinne, Friedensvermittlung, Bruch mit Vereinigten Staaten). 82 base groups fixed (codebook.tsv). Groups 147-576 do not fit No. 205: a second text.

Blind test without the alignment (decode.py --controls, transcription as corrected): proportional position map, a repeated group scores when all its occurrences meet one shared word. Window +-3: tel 205 20/25; telegram No. 212 as control 4/25; part-2 blocks against No. 205 3/19, 2/16, 5/16; 2000 shuffles mean 0.17, max 0.44, none reaching the observed 0.80.

Independent check by a second agent: about 117 groups re-read on full-resolution scans (116 agree; one overtyped figure at group 447 marked [?]); group 40 = 88789 and group 20 = 8918 confirmed; German print re-read; alignment redone blind with own code; spans checked against the transcription. Corrections applied: six-figure group 108609[?] at 377 added to the census; group 20 = 8918; prefix 8 = past participle secure twice, not three times.

Wrote telegram No. 205 as German sentences with holes: words on runs whose split is not fixed (groups 19-23, 28-30, 59-63, 120-121, 125-131), the doubtful 8096, the extra group 7918, the head and the end group are marked. read_share 0.793.
Applied the 82 groups to groups 147-576: 69 of 430 (16.0%) get a value, nearly all function words (ich, daß, hat, auf, für, Wilson, Friedens-). No sentence can be built.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 120 tokens, 87 types, de-modern order 4: reading -2.062 per letter; random keys -2.008 (z -2.1); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -1.809 (mean -1.816, z -29.4); annealer on the real text -1.822. Verdict: underdetermined.

Friedman and Mendelsohn 1938 (archive.org 41766889080599), p. 16 and n. 40: Bernstorff messages via the State Department are in Code 7500, two-part, 10,000 phrases 0000-9999; names nine sibling telegrams; about a dozen in American files. FRUS 1917 Supp. 1 doc. 74: Bernstorff's cover letter says the cipher message refers to the armed-ship question and to the note of 18 Dec on peace terms. Mendelsohn's 1938 paper on Code 7500 not found (NSA Friedman indexes, archive.org).

Looked for sibling Code 7500 ciphertexts to use as cribs: OCR of 14 reels of M367 and M580 for Nov 1916 - Feb 1917, ranking on shared groups; RG 59 bulk OCR; M973 purport lists; Bernstorff name-index cards. Only this cable found; 701.6211/399 (24 Nov 1916) listed but its file is not digitised. Also 862.20212/0-350 and 862.20211/0-200, 601-1000, 1001-1175: German cipher telegrams in other codes, overlap near chance (9% at most).

Catalogue 635 tested as the crib the first pass named: file copy 841.857/244 (M580 roll 191 frame 0111, image seen) reads only '(Quote German cipher)', delivered to the Ambassador 7 Dec 1916. No ciphertext retained.

align_part2.py: local alignment of the known groups of part 2 against all of Bernstorff 1920: best place is No. 205 itself (shared vocabulary, 14.1), no long run anywhere. English word-anchor scan of Official German Documents II found no candidate either. The second text is not in these prints.
No reading of groups 147-576 attempted beyond the 69 known groups: on a two-part code context cannot fix the 361 others, and a filled-in text would be invented. No value added to the key.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.062; polyphony 0.0; 27 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -1.822. Expected for a whole-word code with 1.38 tokens per type: random keys that swap word values of equal length still give German words, so the letter model cannot separate the reading from a fitted key. The statistical check that fits this code is the blind alignment test in decode.py --controls (16/25 at window 2 against 2/25 for the tel 212 control; 0 of 2000 shuffles reach the observed score).

outcome.method: key recovered based on plaintext from external sources
outcome.method_basis: 82 code groups recovered by aligning groups 0-146 with the German text of telegram No. 205 that Bernstorff printed in 1920; no codebook was used.
outcome.fraction_read_source: decode.py over transcription.txt: 120 of the 577 groups have a value of their own in telegram No. 205 (120 of 147 there, 0.816); the 69 groups of part 2 that match a known group are not counted, since part 2 is not read. reading_tel205.md: read_share 0.793 (research/reading_audit/v2_score.py).
outcome.notes: Contributed by WAINUT (catalogue 657). Not a decipherment of an unknown text for part 1: its German text was printed in 1920; what is new, as far as a light search found (Boghardt 2012 and Room 40 files not checked), is the identification of the ciphertext as telegram No. 205, the transcription and the 82 recovered code groups. Part 2 (430 groups) is a second text in the same code and stays unread.

texts.label: Telegram No. 205, Washington, 10 Jan 1917 (groups 0-146)
texts.summary: Bernstorff reports that he has handed Lansing the German memorandum on armed merchant ships, and warns that acting on it will wreck Wilson's peace mediation and bring a break with the United States unless Berlin waits until agreement is reached in Washington; since Wilson decides everything, he must first read the memorandum. Three weeks later Germany declared unrestricted U-boat warfare and the United States broke off relations.

texts.label: Second text, groups 147-576
texts.note: Only the 82 groups fixed by telegram No. 205 are filled in (69 of 430 groups); no sentence can be built and no plaintext is claimed.
texts.summary: A second text in the same code, sent with No. 205. Lansing's letter of 10 Jan 1917 (FRUS 1917 Supp. 1 doc. 75) says Bernstorff's cipher message concerned the armament of Entente merchant ships and also the American note of 18 Dec 1916 on peace terms; this part is probably the second subject. Not confirmed.
